# Task: Support property-to-property comparisons in Cypher WHERE clauses

## Problem

The Cypher query subset supported by `src/cypher/cypher.c` fails to parse a WHERE condition that compares one variable's property with another variable's property. The query aborts with `expected value at pos N` at the right-hand operand.

Examples that fail on the current code:

```
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.name <> b.name RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name
```

Property-to-literal comparisons already work and must keep working:

```
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE b.file_path = 'demo.go' RETURN a.name, b.name
```

## Required behavior

Extend the WHERE parser and evaluator so that when the right-hand side of a comparison operator is another `variable.property` expression (not a string/number/boolean literal), the condition compares the two resolved property values for the current binding.

1. `a.prop = b.prop` — true when the two resolved string values are equal.
2. `a.prop <> b.prop` — true when the two resolved string values differ.
3. All existing comparison operators that make sense on property values (`>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`) should also accept a property right-hand side, evaluated the same way as when the right-hand side is a numeric literal (via `strtod`).
4. The property right-hand side must resolve through the same binding mechanism used for the left-hand side (`node_prop` / bare-alias name), so File, Function, and other node property paths all work.
5. Property-to-literal and bare-alias comparisons must continue to work exactly as before.
6. The change must work in both the early WHERE (after MATCH) and post-WITH WHERE paths, since they share the same parser and evaluator.

## Where to change

- Parser: `parse_condition_expr` in `src/cypher/cypher.c` currently rejects a non-literal right-hand side with `expected value at pos %d`.
- Condition model: `cbm_condition_t` in `src/cypher/cypher.h` currently only stores a literal `value`.
- Evaluator: `eval_condition` / `resolve_condition_value` in `src/cypher/cypher.c` currently resolve only the left-hand side against the binding.

## Constraints

- Do not break any existing Cypher behavior (WHERE with literals, regex, CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, HAS_LABEL, EXISTS, AND/OR/XOR/NOT).
- Keep the error path for genuinely unsupported right-hand sides (e.g. function calls on the RHS if not already supported) clear and non-crashing.
- Add unit tests in the existing Cypher test suite covering property-to-property `=`, `<>`, and at least one ordering operator, plus a WITH-path case.
- The full project test suite (`make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= test`) must still pass.

## How to verify

```sh
make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= cbm
./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli index_repository '{"repo_path":"/tmp/demo","mode":"full","name":"demo"}'
./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli query_graph '{"project":"demo","query":"MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name"}'
```

Before the fix this errors with `expected value at pos N`. After the fix it returns only CALLS edges whose source and target files are the same.

I have investigated the Cypher parser, condition AST, evaluator, and `WITH` projection handling in [src/cypher/cypher.h](file:///Volumes/Projects/a4c/benchmarks/large-repo-comparison/results/2026-10-16-a4c-antigravity-gemini/repo/.a4c/worktrees/task-1792155112536254000/tree/src/cypher/cypher.h) and [src/cypher/cypher.c](file:///Volumes/Projects/a4c/benchmarks/large-repo-comparison/results/2026-10-16-a4c-antigravity-gemini/repo/.a4c/worktrees/task-1792155112536254000/tree/src/cypher/cypher.c). Below is the delegation proposal for implementing and testing property-to-property comparisons in Cypher `WHERE` clauses.

```json
{"proposals": [{"proposal_id": "cypher-prop-to-prop-where", "proposed_agent_id": "coder", "objective": "Support property-to-property (and variable/alias-to-variable/alias) comparisons in Cypher WHERE clauses.

## Target Files
- `src/cypher/cypher.h` (`cbm_condition_t` struct)
- `src/cypher/cypher.c` (`expr_free`, `free_where`, `parse_condition_expr`, `resolve_condition_value`, `eval_condition`, and `execute_with_simple`)
- `tests/test_cypher.c` (unit tests for property-to-property WHERE comparisons)

## Exact Contract
1. **Condition AST (`src/cypher/cypher.h` & cleanup in `src/cypher/cypher.c`)**:
   - Extend `cbm_condition_t` with right-hand side variable/property fields (e.g. `const char *rhs_variable; const char *rhs_property;`).
   - Free `rhs_variable` and `rhs_property` via `safe_str_free` in both `expr_free` and `free_where`.
2. **Parser (`parse_condition_expr` in `src/cypher/cypher.c`)**:
   - After parsing the comparison operator (`c.op`), if the next token is `TOK_IDENT` (and not followed by `TOK_LPAREN`, so unsupported function calls on the RHS still fail cleanly with `expected value at pos %d`):
     - Consume the identifier into `c.rhs_variable`.
     - If followed by `TOK_DOT`, consume the dot and `expect(p, TOK_IDENT)` into `c.rhs_property` (cleaning up and returning `NULL` if the property identifier is missing).
     - Otherwise leave `c.rhs_property = NULL` (bare alias / post-WITH variable on RHS).
3. **Evaluator (`resolve_condition_value` & `eval_condition` in `src/cypher/cypher.c`)**:
   - Factor or generalize `resolve_condition_value` so any `(variable, property)` pair can be resolved against `binding_t *b` using the exact same lookup rules (edge variable via `binding_get_edge` + `edge_prop`, node variable via `binding_get` + `node_prop(n, prop, b->store)` when `prop != NULL`, or `n->name ? n->name : ""` when `prop == NULL`).
   - In `eval_condition`, when `c->rhs_variable != NULL`, resolve the RHS value against `b`. If either LHS or RHS variable is unbound (`NULL`), return `true` (so early WHERE during initial single-node scan in `execute_single` does not prematurely filter out bindings before relationships/additional patterns are expanded, matching existing LHS unbound behavior).
   - Note: `node_prop` and `edge_prop` use rotating buffers of size 8, so resolving LHS and then RHS into separate pointers (or copying if needed) is safe, and pass the resolved RHS string to `eval_comparison_op(c->op, actual, expected)`.
4. **Simple WITH node ID preservation (`execute_with_simple` in `src/cypher/cypher.c`)**:
   - In `execute_with_simple` (around line 3665), when an item is a bare node variable (`!wc->items[ci].property && !wc->items[ci].func && !wc->items[ci].kase && wc->items[ci].variable`), look up `cbm_node_t *gn = binding_get(&bindings[bi], wc->items[ci].variable);` and if `gn && gn->id > 0 && vb.var_count > 0`, set `vb.var_nodes[vb.var_count - 1].id = gn->id;` (matching `execute_with_aggregate` line 3644). This ensures `MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name` re-fetches `a.file_path` and `b.file_path` via `node_prop` instead of comparing empty strings.

## Constraints
- Do not break any existing Cypher behavior (WHERE with literals, regex, CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, HAS_LABEL, EXISTS, AND/OR/XOR/NOT).
- Keep the error path (`expected value at pos %d`) for unsupported RHS tokens (including function calls like `foo()`).
- Add unit tests in `tests/test_cypher.c` covering property-to-property `=`, `<>`, at least one ordering operator (`<`, `>`, `<=`, or `>=`), and a `WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path` case.

## Verification
- Run `make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= test` and ensure all tests pass.", "budget_tokens": 30000}]}
```
